The military signal degradation has been shut off. The entire continent just cleared up to within ten meters.

We brought C.I.P.H.E.R. online to catalog coordinate vaults inside decommissioned rocket-motor testing casings along the corridor. If R.S.I. road workers or retired steel fabricators inspect these junction boxes, they will only see overbuilt steel scrap.

R.S.I. FACILITY RETIREMENT SWEEP // CREW 4 (DAVE & MACK)
OBJECT: Relic Relay Housing #04 (Solid Rocket Motor Test Corridor)

Inspected junction box welded to the I-beam in 1987.
- Casing: 1/4-inch rolled steel. Zero deflection. Welds pristine.
- Gasket: Holding fine, smells faintly of sulfur and burnt solid fuel.
- Internal: Some clown stuffed an old green circuit board inside.
  Mack tried to pry it loose with a 24-inch pipe wrench, but the board
  let out a weird buzzing squeal through the ground rod.
  We figured it was a stray 12V trickle from the old igniter lines.

Left it alone. Not our job to scrap microchips. Box stamped PASS.
Bolted shut with four 3/4-inch grade-8 hex bolts. Torqued to 90 ft-lbs.
